# Wolfpack

> Wolfpack is a self-hosted control room for persistent coding-agent terminals on your own machines.

Wolfpack provides PWA and CLI control of long-running terminal sessions from a phone or browser.

Built-in coding-agent provider choices: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Pi.

Shell is the always-available fallback. Custom commands and wrappers on PATH are supported separately. Sessions run locally through a Rust PTY broker; Wolfpack does not provide a hosted relay or account service. Remote access is typically handled through Tailscale.

## Primary links

- Canonical homepage: https://get-wolfpack.netlify.app/

## Core topics

- Persistent coding-agent terminals on operator-controlled machines
- Browser terminal dashboard
- Mobile control for persistent terminal sessions
- Self-hosted remote development over Tailscale
- Persistent PTY sessions owned by a local broker
- Multi-machine session list and desktop terminal grid

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/almogdepaz/wolfpack/main/install.sh | bash
```

The installer immediately launches setup. After setup, if you accepted the login service, open the printed URL. If you declined the login service, run `wolfpack`, then open the printed URL. In either case, run `wolfpack doctor` to verify the installation.

Package runners:

```bash
bunx wolfpack-bridge@latest
npx --yes wolfpack-bridge@latest
```

Package runners do not add `wolfpack` to `PATH`; repeat the runner prefix for every later command.

See [installation details](https://github.com/almogdepaz/wolfpack/blob/main/docs/installation.md) for the complete installation procedure.

## Security model summary

Wolfpack is self-hosted software for machines you control. Treat access to Wolfpack like shell access to that machine. The browser talks to the local Wolfpack server over HTTP/WebSocket, the server talks to the broker over a per-user Unix socket, and the broker owns PTYs and runs commands locally in selected project directories. Optional JWT auth can be layered on top of Tailscale.
